Issued at 241 PM EDT Sun Aug 30 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level high pressure over the southern and up 
to the central US will remain in place today, with shortwave energy 
traversing across the Florida peninsula. At the surface, the ridge 
axis over the western Atlantic will remain north of the Florida 
peninsula. Locally, easterly flow will persist, both at the surface 
and aloft. This will allow the east coast sea breeze to push farther 
inland once again this afternoon. Moisture across the local area 
will remain above normal, with PW values of 2.0-2.2". This will 
support scattered to numerous showers and storms this afternoon (PoP 
40-70%). Scattered showers and storms have already pushed onshore 
along the coast, primarily from Cape Canaveral southward), with 
additional storms forming along outflow boundaries as this activity 
pushes inland. Local guidance continues to show activity 
increasing and focusing across the interior this afternoon and 
early evening. Highest coverage of storms will occur across the 
interior, in association with the sea breeze collision late this 
afternoon and into this evening. 

The environment supports this higher coverage of storms, with plenty 
of instability (MUCAPE 1500-2000 J/kg), ample buoyancy (lifted index 
of -4 to -6), fairly cold aloft (-7C at 500 mb), and sufficient 
downdraft potential (DCAPE 600-700 J/kg). Main storm hazards will be 
frequent lightning, gusty winds of 45-55 mph, with a very low (less 
than 2%) chance for isolated damaging winds around 60 mph, small 
hail, and heavy rainfall of 2-3" (with up to a 5% chance for mounts 
over 4"), which may lead to minor localized flooding. The Weather 
Prediction Center (WPC) has outlined all of east central Florida 
into a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 4) for Excessive Rainfall. Any 
lingering activity will diminish shortly after sundown, with 
activity across the Atlantic waters continuing through the overnight 
hours. Some of this activity may push onshore through the night, 
with PoP 20-40% lingering along the coast overnight to account for 
this. Temperatures will be near normal, with afternoon highs in the 
upper 80s to low 90s along the coast, and low to mid 90s across the 
interior. These temperatures coupled with humidity will produce peak 
heat indices of 100-107F, which remains below Heat Advisory 
criteria. HeatRisk impacts remain generally Moderate, with a few 
areas of Major in and around the Orlando Metro Area, and along the 
southern coast. Conditions tonight will remain warm and muggy with 
overnight lows in the low to mid 70s. 

Monday-Friday... Upper level high pressure over the southern US will 
slowly shift eastward through the time period. At the surface, high 
pressure over the Atlantic will remain in place, with the ridge axis 
staying north of the Florida peninsula. Locally, deep easterly flow 
will prevail, with speeds generally around 10 mph. This will support 
the development and farther inland progression of the east coast sea 
breeze each afternoon. Moisture across the local area will remain 
near to above normal, with PW values of 1.8-2.1". Daily afternoon 
showers and lightning storms are forecast to continue (PoP 40-70%), 
with scattered storms forming along the advancing east coast sea 
breeze through early afternoon each day, with additional showers and 
storms forming across the interior by mid afternoon into early 
evening. Highest coverage of storms will be across the interior, 
where the sea breeze collision is forecast to occur each evening, 
generally around Orlando westward. Model soundings trend closer 
to the long-skinny profile, resulting in a little less instability
and downdraft enhancement from entrainment, but better supporting
heavy rainfall. Storm hazards will be frequent lightning, gusty 
winds, and locally heavy rainfall, with minor flooding possible in
urban and poor drainage areas. Shower and lightning storm 
activity will diminish into the overnight hours, however, 
scattered showers and storms will continue across the Atlantic 
waters each night. Some of this activity may push onshore along 
the coast in the easterly flow through the night and into the 
morning hours each day (PoP20-40%). 

Temperatures will remain seasonably hot and humid with highs in the 
upper 80s to low 90s along the coast and low to mid 90s across the 
interior. These temperatures coupled with high humidity will produce 
heat indices of 100-106, with up to 108 possible in spots next week. 
A Heat Advisory may be needed for some parts of east central Florida 
next week. Be sure to stay adequately hydrated if spending extended 
periods of time outdoors and also take breaks in the shade or in air 
conditioning to help prevent the development of heat-related 
illness. Overnight lows will continue to be warm and muggy with lows 
in the low to mid 70s.
